# Introduction

The main goals of this lab are for you to 1) get more familiar with the CS01 data and 2) gain familiarity with `dplyr`.

# Getting started

To get started, find your `lab02-<your GitHub username>` repo in the [course GitHub organization](https://github.com/COGS137-FA26), clone the repo (using SSH) into RStudio on datahub. And, then you're ready to go!

# Packages

This lab uses two packages: `tidyverse` (which includes `dplyr`, the package you'll be using most in this lab) and (you may want to use) `janitor` (for `clean_names()`). Both are loaded for you in the `load-packages` chunk of the provided .qmd template.

# Data

The three data files you'll be using in this lab have been provided in the `data/` folder. You'll see the following three lines in the provided .qmd template for this lab, which, when run, will read each of the files into R for you:

``` r
WB <- read_csv("data/Blood.csv")
OF <- read_csv("data/OF.csv")
BR <- read_csv("data/Breath.csv")
```

# Exercises

For each dataset, we want you to start to gain familiarity with the data in there, without having yet been provided much guidance in class. The goal here is to try out as many different `dplyr` functions as possible...while learning things about the data. For each dataset, use *at least* three different `dplyr` functions and state three things you learned about the data while practicing with `dplyr`.
